title: Ken’s First Week in London
author: Tadoku Note (original)
summary: ロンドンのホテルで働き始めたケン。教室の外で英語を使う、はじめての一週間。

source.note: Original text written for this app.

paragraphs: Ken had studied English for six years at school in Osaka, but he had never used it outside the classroom. Now he was standing at Heathrow Airport with two heavy suitcases, and everyone around him was speaking English very fast.
He was going to work at a small hotel in London for one year. The hotel manager, Mrs. Green, had written to him in an email: “Take the Underground to Paddington. I will meet you there.”

The Underground was easy to find, but buying a ticket was not. Ken stood in front of the ticket machine for a long time. A woman behind him asked, “Are you all right, love?” Ken did not understand why she called him “love.” He was very confused, but he said, “Yes, thank you,” and finally pressed the right buttons.
Mrs. Green was waiting at Paddington. She was a tall woman with short gray hair and a warm smile. “Welcome to London!” she said. “Are you hungry? Let’s get you a cup of tea first.”

Over the next few days, Ken learned many things. He learned that people in London often said “Cheers” when they meant “thank you.” He learned that the weather could change four times in one afternoon. He learned that a “queue” was a line of people, and that everyone waited in it patiently.

His job at the hotel was to help guests at the front desk. On the first day, he was very nervous. A guest asked him, “Could you tell me the way to the British Museum?” Ken knew the answer, but his mouth would not move. Mrs. Green stood next to him and waited quietly. Finally, Ken said, “Take the number 7 bus. It is about twenty minutes.” The guest thanked him and left. Ken felt as if he had just climbed a mountain.

In the evenings, Ken walked around the city. He saw red buses and black taxis, old churches and new glass buildings. He sat in parks and listened to people talking. He did not understand everything, but he started to hear the same words and phrases again and again. Slowly, they began to make sense.
On Friday, Mrs. Green asked him, “So, how was your first week?” Ken thought for a moment. “It was difficult,” he said. “But every day was a little easier than the day before.”
Mrs. Green smiled. “That’s how it works,” she said. “You don’t learn a language all at once. You learn it one day at a time.”
That night, Ken wrote an email to his family. For the first time, he wrote it in English.
